newsitem.title: JAPAN: SOCCER-KASHIWA REYSOL LEAD J-LEAGUE FOR FIRST TIME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KASHIWA REYSOL LEAD J-LEAGUE FOR FIRST TIME.

text.p: Kashiwa Reysol went top of Japanese soccer's J-League for the first-ever time on Wednesday with a 1-0 home win over bottom club Nagoya.
Brazilian Edilson scored the only goal, his sixth of the season, in the 10th minute and Kashiwa held on to win an ill-tempered match featuring six yellow cards -- two for Kashiwa and four for Nagoya.

The landmark victory for Kashiwa, playing their third season in the top league, came as newcomers Kobe pulled off a 3-2 upset away win over previous leaders Gamba Osaka, thanks to two goals by veteran striker Akihiro Nagashima.
Cameroon's Patrick Mboma scored an injury-time goal for Gamba, who dominated midfield for much of the game but lacked accuracy in passing and finishing.
Defending champions Kashima won 3-1 at Urawa to climb to second place after losing the leadership with Saturday's shock 4-0 defeat by Kashiwa.
Jorginho, Yutaka Akita and Yoshiyuki Hasegawa found the net as the Antlers moved up from fourth place to trail Kashiwa on goal difference with a game in hand.

Brazilian Dunga broke a 1-1 stalemate in the 75th minute as pre-season favorites Iwata beat visiting Yokohama Flugels 3-1 to sneak into third spot in the 17-club table after seven games in the first-stage competition.
Masaaki Sawanobori's strike and an own goal in the first half helped Shimizu to a 2-1 win over Hiratsuka at Tokyo's National Stadium and to fourth place with its fourth victory in a row.

Japanese international Hiroaki Morishima blasted home a vital second-half goal to lead Cerezo Osaka to a 2-1 win at struggling Kawasaki, who missed key international forward Kazuyoshi Miura for the sixth straight match due to a sprained ankle.
Elsewhere, hosts Kyoto edged Fukuoka 1-0 on a goal by Brazilian Daniel, and Ichihara overcame Hiroshima 3-2 with a sudden-death extra-time goal by Yugoslav midfielder Nenad Maslovar.
